sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Long Beach, NY?
sections.html:
Long Beach sellers can list on the open market, sell privately, or take a cash purchase with no repair requests, and the barrier-island setting is part of the story for each of them, since Hurricane Sandy flooded the city in 2012. Condition and documentation carry real weight here.

  • Agent listing: fits updated homes in strong blocks and sellers who can wait through a buyer's inspection and flood insurance quote.
  • For sale by owner: you run showings and negotiate, and your attorney prepares the contract and deed.
  • Cash buyer: fits a damaged bungalow, an inherited house or a rental you no longer want, since the purchase is as-is.

Before choosing, line up your survey, any elevation certificate, insurance claim history and permit records. Those papers answer the first questions any Long Beach buyer asks.

sections.h2: What makes Long Beach different from other Nassau County places?
sections.html:
Long Beach is a dense oceanfront city on a barrier island, with the Atlantic to the south and Reynolds Channel to the north. It covers 2.22 square miles of land, is less than a mile wide and about 3.5 miles long, and ranks among the densest communities in the country. Fewer than 40% of its homes are detached houses, so apartments, condos and attached homes account for much of the housing.

The city began as a resort. It became an incorporated village in 1913 and a city in 1922, and developer William H. Reynolds promoted it as the "Riviera of the East." Hurricane Sandy hit on October 29, 2012, causing more than $250 million in damage and leaving the city without power and running water for two weeks. The 2.2-mile boardwalk was rebuilt for about $44 million and fully reopened on October 25, 2013.

Neighborhoods vary a lot in feel and housing type:

  • West End: small bungalows and a few large houses on narrow streets that run from beach to bay.
  • East End: wider land between ocean and bay, with larger family houses.
  • The Canals and The Walks: canal-front streets and a network of narrow walkways between houses.
  • Central District and North Park: the area around City Hall and the Long Island Rail Road terminal.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Long Beach housing?
sections.html:
Long Beach has a median owner-occupied home value of $696,400 and about 15,000 households, and only 66.0% of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $2,515. The table gathers the Census QuickFacts numbers that matter most to a seller.

The long mean commute fits the city's role as a commuter community. The Long Beach branch of the Long Island Rail Road ends at a terminal at Park Place and Park Avenue, and the city runs its own 24-hour bus service. The Long Beach City School District serves the city, with a pre-kindergarten, four elementary schools, a middle school and a high school.

sections.h2: Which permits does the Long Beach Building Department require?
sections.html:
The Long Beach Building Department requires a permit for a long list of home work, and an unpermitted job in your house history can slow a sale. Its permit page lists roofs, siding, fences, driveways and curb cuts, central heating and air conditioning, sidewalks, bulkheads and docks, decks and porches, pools, hot tubs and saunas, fireplaces and chimneys, and all plumbing. All electrical work must be done by a licensed electrician, and a dumpster or roll-off container placed on the street needs a permit as well.

Additions, alterations and new structures also need approval, as does cutting a wall, removing a beam or changing a stairway or required exit. The department sits on the third floor of City Hall. Permit prices change, so ask the office for the current fee before you start work. If you did a bulkhead, deck or roof after Sandy, pull your permit and final inspection records now and keep them with your closing file.

sections.h2: How do Long Beach city taxes get billed and paid?
sections.html:
The city's Tax Department bills City of Long Beach real estate tax and residential sanitation, and it also bills and collects the current-year Nassau County tax. That makes one office the contact for most of your property tax questions. Payment is accepted on the third floor of City Hall in cash or by check, by mail to the City of Long Beach Treasurer at 1 West Chester Street, or online.

The City Charter lets properties with annual city taxes under $8,000 pay in two installments, while a bill of $8,000 or more is due in one payment in July. The Tax Department notice for the FY2027 bills says properties between $7,000 and $8,000 were mistakenly billed as a single July payment, and that the Superblock Deficit line item is wrong on every bill even though the total due is correct.

If an escrow account pays your tax, the notice warns that a lender may keep collecting as if two installments still apply after a property crosses into the single-payment group. Ask your servicer to review the escrow before closing, and ask the Tax Department for a written balance so your attorney can adjust it at the closing table.

sections.h2: Can I grieve a Long Beach assessment through Nassau County?
sections.html:
Not for the city's own assessment. Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission says that if the City of Long Beach assesses your property, you appeal to the city's Board of Assessment Review, and a filing with the commission does not preserve your rights there. The county's filing window for its own tentative roll runs from January 4 to March 1, 2027, with no fee and no extension, and applies to county-assessed properties.

The county FAQ also notes that the commission can only lower an assessment or leave it as is. Ask the City of Long Beach assessor for the grievance dates and forms that apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a Long Beach house?
sections.html:
New York State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of the sale price, rounded up, and the seller owes it unless the contract says otherwise. On the city's $696,400 median value that is about $2,788. The buyer pays the 1% mansion tax if a residential price reaches $1 million. The state's transfer tax page says the TP-584 return and payment go to the county clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

The Nassau County Clerk records deeds and lists recording fees on its real estate records pages. Ask your attorney or title company for the exact recording charge on your closing statement. After the sale, close your STAR registration, as the state's STAR page directs.

faqs.q: Does Nassau County assess my Long Beach house?
faqs.a: Not always. If the City of Long Beach assesses your property, you appeal to the city's own review board, and Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission filing does not cover that city assessment.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Long Beach?
faqs.a: The city's Tax Department bills City of Long Beach real estate tax and residential sanitation and also bills the current-year Nassau County tax. You can pay at City Hall, by mail to the City Treasurer or online.

faqs.q: Is my Long Beach city tax paid in one payment or two?
faqs.a: Properties with annual city taxes under $8,000 may pay in two installments, and $8,000 or more is due in one payment in July. The city's notice says some bills between $7,000 and $8,000 were wrongly issued as a single payment.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work on my Long Beach house?
faqs.a: Yes for most structural, mechanical and exterior work. The Building Department lists roofs, siding, fences, driveways, decks, pools, heating and cooling, plumbing and electrical work, and street dumpsters among the items that need a permit.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Long Beach sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes New York State's $2 per $500 transfer tax unless the contract shifts it, and the buyer owes the 1% mansion tax when a residential price is $1 million or more.
